issues.cell: law 2 *Carried way* (stage 1: 'a pick §4.2 S3 (4) forces there, counted in N₁ ... law 2 (c) where S3 (4) can force none ... the way never moved, else law 2 (c)') × S3 (4)'s pick contour and forced-pick order × S3 (6)–(7) × law 2 (b) × *held*
issues.claim: A drawn (unlocked) or kept (placement-locked) raised road's carried way at stage 1: the pick is forced at S3 (4), where only the pick contour exists, while S3 (7)'s gate falls where T = t_1 crosses the way — on the ramp (R7-03 (a) re-solves a way 'never moved', or the gate goes beyond the foot), on the deck (the later trace passes beneath, no gate needed, N₁ − 1 gates or a re-drawn/dropped forced pick), or nowhere; where the pick contour meets only the deck, 'S3 (4) can force none' sends stage 1 to law 2 (c). The carried way's place in S3 (4)'s forced-pick order (polycentric, harbour, several ways) is unsaid: with one unforced pick left, a walled or an unwalled stage 1. And 'never moved, else law 2 (c)' (PRB7D-GEN-07, pre-J148) skips (b) for an unlocked or placement-locked way that *held*, J147 (1) and J144 move (re-routed through a stage gate, as by hand). PRB7F-GEN-05's closure fails in part.
issues.required_change: Part L *Carried way*: '(at stage 1 a pick §4.2 S3 (4) forces there, counted in N₁, the way standing for its route (5) and S3 (7)'s gate on it, law 2 (c) where S3 (4) can force none; at a stage k ≥ 2 a pin of S5a there, one of S5b's c; ...), the way never moved, else law 2 (c)' → '(at stage 1, once S3 (6) has fixed the boundary, a gate S3 (7) places at the first point beyond the foot where the boundary crosses that way's ground course — a gate of the stage not counted in N₁, as the harbour gate is not, the ways taken in address order, and none where the boundary crosses only the deck, which the trace then passes beneath (law 1 (3)); at a stage k ≥ 2 a pin of S5a there, one of S5b's c), and where that stage's gate law can give it no lawful gate there (a closed arc, a footprint in a strip), the way — unless shape-locked — re-routed by law 2 (b), by §4.3's router from the first point beyond the foot through the nearest gate of that trace a way of its class may pass, its two ends kept, a placement-locked way's change shown by law 4's (G2), else law 2 (c)'; veto 12 'counted in the stage's' → 'beside the stage's count at stage 1, as the harbour gate is, and one of c at a stage k ≥ 2'; §5.3's gate row, §4.3 *Routes*' roads-leaving count and F-WALL's 'fewer arterial crossings than N' add 'and any gate a carried way takes (§2.7's laws, law 2 *Carried way*)'. (Alternative keeping N₁: the pick forced on the pick contour at the way's first crossing beyond the foot, after the polycentric and harbour forced picks and before every unforced pick, the ways in address order; S3 (7)'s gate at the first point beyond the foot where T = t_1 crosses its ground course, none and the pick dropped (N₁ reported short) where T = t_1 crosses only its deck; the same law 2 (b) clause.)

issues.cell: law 2 (a) 'planned round every Tier-1 thing standing as the commit began that it does not lay again' (PRB7F-LCK-03) × *Not yet built* × *commit* (each stage) × law 1 (11) × *Newer*
issues.claim: At generation the stage-1 gates and water gates (fixed by S3, laid by S5a for k = 1, after S4), a castle's town-side gate and vertex towers (fixed by its claim, laid by S7) and every anchor's tower (S7) stand at no commit S4 or S6 begins, so by law 2 (a)'s words S4's viaduct and S6's aqueduct plan round none of them; *Not yet built* only says how a step reads a part when it reads it. Builder 1 ignores them, and the stage that lays them (the op's own by *Newer*) moves them along their tie by law 2 (a) — S5a moving an S3-fixed water gate off S3 (10)'s moat deck and S4's split routes though it 'commits this trace unchanged', S7 re-siting a castle by law 2 (c) after S4–S6 built round it — or, by 'builds exactly that', §5.3's row aborts; builder 2 reads *Not yet built* into (a), as R7-02's fixed-place sentence ('S6's aqueduct reads the fixed places the trace and the castle record before S7 lays their towers') does. Law 1 (11) cannot see the move (the thing did not stand as that commit began). Generation member of PRB7G-TIM-03's class.
issues.required_change: Part L law 2 (a): 'planned round every Tier-1 thing standing as the commit began that it does not lay again' → 'planned round every Tier-1 thing standing as the commit began, laid earlier in it, or not yet built with its place fixed by an earlier step of its event (*Not yet built*: a stage's gates, water gates and anchors with their towers from the step that fixed them, a castle's fixed places from its claim's commit), that it does not lay again'; *Not yet built*, after 'and the step that builds it builds exactly that': '— never moving it for a meeting, law 1 (11) and the check reading it as standing from the step that fixed its place'; law 1 (11): 'no gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing as a commit begins' → 'no gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing as a commit begins, or fixed by an earlier step of its event (*Not yet built*),'.

issues.cell: law 1 (2), (5), (7)'s 'the wall's top' (no term) × *the band*'s 'along its stretch profile' × *Not yet built* ('when a step reads it') × the check at every stage end × S7's Enceinte.base, heightCm, thicknessCm, stretchClass
issues.claim: From a trace's commit (S5a) to S7's, no record holds the wall's top or its graded band: S7 writes the base knots, the height and the stretch class (absent until then = 'full throughout'), while law 1 binds at every stage end between (S5a–S5d, S6) and 'the wall's top', which law 1 (2) has turned on since pass 6 (PRB7F-GEN-03), is defined nowhere. Reading (A), what stands (the full curtain on the ground, as *the band* and the support step's (3) read it), and (B), *Not yet built* (the parapet S7 will write on its base knots), give different S6 aqueducts and S5a traces: an aqueduct over a parapet arc planned by (B) fails §5.3's row at S6's end (channel above the full top, soffit below it: neither form); planned by (A) it is merged, and at S7's end the parapet makes it neither form with no lawful outcome; a station slid off the parapet band stands in the full band; a pull keeping an S4 viaduct's foot clear by the parapet strips' width fails law 1 (4) at S5a's end. On uneven ground terrain vs S7's linear base knots splits any crossing near a form's boundary.
issues.required_change: Part L Terms, after *the wall strips*: '**The wall's top** at a point is its base there plus the height of its section there (the rows *the band* names, along its stretch profile); the cap law 1 (7) reads beneath a road deck is a reading of it, never it. From the commit that lays a wall's line to the commit that writes its section — at generation, a regeneration and an epoch's new walled stage S7's (base, heightCm, thicknessCm, walkCm, stretchClass; §4.8) — its band, wall strips, top and walk, and its gates' and towers' heights and footprints, are read, by every step, by law 1 and by the check alike, as that commit will write them from what stands (*Not yet built*: the stretch profile from the arcs the trace's classification graded, the base from the ground at the trace's vertices), and that commit writes exactly that.' The check, after 'each clause from what the commit leaves': '— a section or part a later commit of its event writes read as *Not yet built* reads it —'; *Not yet built*: 'when a step reads it' → 'when a step, law 1 or the check reads it'. (Narrower alternative: law 1 (2), (4)'s widths, (5) and (7) bind a wall from the commit that writes its section, as law 1 (8) binds a chamber from the vaults step.)

issues.cell: law 2 (a) 'lawfully — ... a way through a gate's passage by §4.3's crossing rule among them' (PRB7F-LCK-06) × veto 6 ('a gate's way passing square beneath'), correction 7 × §4.3's crossing rule ('laid after it') × the support step's (3), *The clearance* × J149's OVER
issues.claim: S6's aqueduct (newer) over a standing main gate whose arterial, laid before it, passes at 40° to the deck, the arch clearing gatehouse and wall: builder 1 reads the crossing rule (with PRB7F-LCK-06's decision and veto 6) as binding whichever came first and bends the aqueduct until the gate's way passes square, else off the gate, else not built — so a generated aqueduct seldom passes over a gate; builder 2 reads 'among them' as among the newer's own derivation's rules (§4.3 binds ways laid after a raised way; a raised way laid over a standing way clears it at any angle) and keeps the course, as J149's OVER admits. Law 1 (5) reads no way, so §5.3's row passes both; a later regeneration re-deriving the ring under the kept aqueduct bars the same gate under one reading only.
issues.required_change: Part L law 2 (a): 'a way through a gate's passage by §4.3's crossing rule among them' → 'a way laid after a raised way through a gate's passage beneath it by §4.3's crossing rule among them — a raised way laid over a standing gate meeting that gate's way as it meets any standing way (the support step's (3) and *The clearance*), never by the crossing rule'; veto 6 'a gate's way passing square beneath' → 'a gate's way laid after the aqueduct passing square beneath'; correction 7 'a gate's way passing by §4.3's crossing rule' → 'a gate's way laid after the aqueduct passing by §4.3's crossing rule'. (Alternative: '… among them, whichever was laid first — a raised way laid over a standing gate bending until that gate's way crosses its strip by §4.3's crossing rule, else planning round the gate (law 2 (a), (c))', veto 6 naming the narrowing of J149's 'may pass over a gate' as the program's reading.)

issues.cell: the Terms' union of strips × law 1 (5)'s 'but in an aqueduct's crossing law 1 (2) reads over whose every span over it clears its top' × law 1 (2), (7)'s top ('the lowest soffit there'; 'beneath an aqueduct the wall keeps its own top')
issues.claim: A stage ring beneath an S4 viaduct where S6's aqueduct crosses it at the same place (strips overlapping, or stacked), S7 laying a spacing tower there: read on the union, law 1 (5)'s exception admits a footprint in the aqueduct's clearing over crossing whole — a tower under a road deck's span, against veto 6 and J149 ('viaducts … unchanged'); read per raised way, the viaduct's strip bars it. Where the band lies beneath both spans, (7) caps it at the road deck's soffit or at the lower aqueduct soffit, against 'beneath an aqueduct the wall keeps its own top', and (2) reads the aqueduct's form against the own top (merged or neither) or the capped one (over). Two towers, tops and forms at one crossing; same union class as PRB7G-LCK-04 at law 1 (4).
issues.required_change: Part L law 1 (5): 'but in an aqueduct's crossing law 1 (2) reads over whose every span over it clears its top' → 'but where it lies in no road deck's strip and in an aqueduct's crossing law 1 (2) reads over, every standing span of every raised way over it clearing its top'; law 1 (7): 'no higher than the lowest soffit there' → 'no higher than the lowest soffit of a road deck there, whatever aqueduct stands over it too'; law 1 (2)'s 'the wall's top' read as the wall's own top, the cap of law 1 (7) a reading beside it (the term PRB7G-GEN-03 adds).

issues.cell: R7-02 *beneath*'s list of the pull's impassables (example) × law 1 (3), (4) × E-P9
issues.claim: R7-02 *beneath* gives a closed list of what a pulled or cost-field trace (S3's and S5a's at generation and a regeneration) treats as impassable — ramps, stairs and feet widened, an aqueduct's supports, held buildings' strips — without a road deck's strip but to cross its deck line (law 1 (4), PRB7F-LCK-05) or the deck line of a road deck dated after the stage's boundary pick (law 1 (3), *Order*: S3 (7)'s stretches at stage 1, the stage's own S5b decks); E-P9 carries both at §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2), but the worked example the model writes at §2.7 (E-M1) does not, and corrections 3, 6 and 7 reach ramps, shape-locked spans and aqueducts only.
issues.required_change: R7-02 *beneath*: 'and every held building's widened strip (below) as impassable to its line' → 'and every held building's widened strip (below) as impassable to its line, with a road deck's strip but to cross its deck line once and the deck line of every road deck dated after the stage's boundary pick (§2.7's laws, law 1 (3), (4); the list §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2) gives)'.
